profile.name: HOPE Clinic

existing_offices.name: HOPE Aldine

profile.free_text:
[hc_status] What kind of health center are you: Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC)
[payers] Which payers do you see, and roughly what share of patients is each: Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare and commercial plans; uninsured patients on a sliding fee. Shares not stated.
[service_area] Is the new site part of a grant or HRSA service area: Greater Houston: Harris and Fort Bend counties. Avoid overlapping other health centers' service areas.
[client_travel] How do patients reach you: Mix
[partners] Which partners refer patients or share space: Website: partnered with Houston Methodist for pulmonology; a school-based clinic in Aldine ISD (Aldine Meadows).
[visibility] How much does being seen from the road matter: Helps, not essential
[tenure] Would you lease, buy or build: Not sure

profile.name: Baylor College of Medicine
profile.free_text:
[customer_origin] Where do your customers come from today: Our offices are in Upper Kirby (77098), River Oaks (77027), and the Texas Medical Center (77030). These are office ZIP codes, not verified patient-origin ZIP codes. Patient origins and travel times are unknown. Proposed planning catchment: approximately 15–20 minutes for routine primary care, with a separate transit-access analysis. Search Harris, Fort Bend, and Montgomery counties and account for overlap with our existing practices.
[referrals] Where do referrals come from: Actual referral shares are unknown. Proposed acquisition channels to evaluate: patients scheduling directly, recommendations from existing patients, Baylor specialty practices referring patients for ongoing primary care, and hospital-discharge follow-up. Map Baylor affiliates as potential care-coordination relationships, while verifying actual referral arrangements
[clinicians] How many clinicians per location: 6
[competitors] Who do you compete with, or who else serves the same people: Evaluate nearby Kelsey-Seybold primary-care clinics, Houston Methodist Primary Care Group, and independent family-medicine/internal-medicine practices. Compare their services and accepted plans before treating them as interchangeable alternatives. Kelsey-Seybold offers family medicine, internal medicine, and pediatrics; Houston Methodist operates a primary-care network. Also map community health centers as existing access points and potential coordination partners. Identify Baylor’s own relevant clinics separately when estimating overlap.
[space] Anything else the space must have: Proposed neighborhood outpatient clinic of 6,000–10,000 square feet, preferably an existing medical buildout with approximately 12 exam rooms, phlebotomy/specimen space, a small procedure room, private counseling space, reception, and staff support areas. Require accessible entrances and restrooms, convenient drop-off, and patient parking. Use $35/sf/year as a provisional base-rent screening ceiling; show operating expenses, tenant improvements, and other occupancy costs separately. Proposed operating hours: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–6:30 p.m., with staggered staffing. Confirm medical use and buildout feasibility before treating any listing as suitable.
